prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Conservatives’ 2015 Manifesto sets out a long-term plan to secure a better future for you, your family and Britain—rewarding work, strengthening the economy, protecting vital services and defending our country.

- Strong economy first: eliminate the deficit and then run a surplus to keep taxes and mortgages low; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance; raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000; crack down on avoidance and evasion; back a dynamic, competitive economy across all regions with a Northern Powerhouse, elected metro mayors and major infrastructure (HS2/HS3, road upgrades, Crossrail, real-terms frozen commuter fares, universal broadband, better mobile and 5G).

- Jobs and enterprise: aim for full employment and 2 million more jobs; create 3 million new apprenticeships; cut £10bn more red tape; keep the UK’s competitive business taxes; review business rates; treble Start Up Loans; boost exports and innovation, science and advanced manufacturing.

- Fair taxes and welfare that make work pay: cut income tax for 30 million; a Tax‑Free Minimum Wage law so no one working 30 hours on the Minimum Wage pays Income Tax; roll out Universal Credit; lower the household benefit cap to £23,000; freeze most working‑age benefits for two years (with key exemptions); Youth Allowance with tougher work requirements; targeted support for those with treatable conditions.

- Controlled immigration that benefits Britain: keep net migration in the tens of thousands; reform EU welfare—four‑year residency before tax credits/child benefit, end jobseeker benefits, residency rules for social housing; tougher deportations and illegal working enforcement; Modern Slavery Act; Controlling Migration Fund.

- World‑class education: zero tolerance for failure; core academic subjects; tougher primary standards; turn every failing/coasting school into an academy; open 500 new free schools; protect per‑pupil funding (plus pupil premium); recruit more top teachers, especially in maths/physics; expand UTCs and apprenticeships; lift cap on university places and introduce postgraduate loans.

- A strong, patient‑centred NHS: increase NHS spending every year and provide at least £8bn extra by 2020; deliver a truly 7‑day NHS with 7‑day GP access (same‑day for over‑75s); named GP, digital records and online services; improve mental health access and cancer survival; integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs.

- Homes and ownership: keep mortgage rates lower; extend Help to Buy and launch the Help to Buy ISA; build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount) for under‑40s; extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; brownfield first; protect the Green Belt.

- Energy and environment: keep bills down via competition and smart meters; back safe shale with community benefits; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give locals the final say; meet climate goals cost‑effectively; protect countryside and forests, expand Marine Conservation Zones and a global “Blue Belt,” invest in flood defences.

- Law, order and liberty: finish police reform; modernise prisons and rehabilitation; tougher sentencing where needed; a new Victims’ Law; combat violence against women and girls; scrap the Human Rights Act and introduce a British Bill of Rights.

- Security and global influence: retain Trident; maintain strong, modern Armed Forces and reserves; equip our military properly; counter extremism (including non‑violent) with new powers; uphold NATO; meet the 0.7% aid commitment to save lives, build stability and open markets.

- Our Union and sovereignty: implement new Scottish and Welsh powers; English votes for English laws (including English rates of Income Tax); strengthen Northern Ireland’s settlement; hold an in‑out EU referendum by the end of 2017; keep the pound and reform the EU to be more competitive and less intrusive.

- Big Society and family: guarantee a place on National Citizen Service; three days’ paid volunteering for workers in large firms and the public sector; support marriage and families; 30 hours of free childcare for working parents of 3- and 4‑year‑olds.

This is a clear Conservative plan to reward those who work hard and do the right thing, protect the vulnerable, and keep Britain secure, prosperous and free.
